data.gender_notes: Mazloomun is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is unfortunate, wretched, or afflicted with misfortune. The name Mazloomun carries the meaning “Unfortunate, Wretched” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu. Parents who choose Mazloomun usually hope their child will grow to embody unfortunate, wretched and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Mazloomun belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Unfortunate, Wretched.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mazloomun total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_english.name: Mazloomun
in_english.meaning: Children of God who suffer from oppression and injustice
in_english.long_meaning: Mazloomun is a name that refers to the children of God who suffer from oppression and injustice. The Arabic root of the name mazloomun means to be oppressed or to suffer from injustice. In Islamic tradition, the name mazloomun is associated with the concept of being a victim of oppression and injustice. The name mazloomun is also associated with the idea of seeking refuge in God from oppression and injustice. In Islamic theology, the name mazloomun is used to refer to the children of God who are oppressed and unjustly treated. The name mazloomun is also used to refer to the children of God who are suffering from hunger, thirst, and poverty. In Islamic tradition, the name mazloomun is considered a name of great spiritual significance and is often given to children who are born into families that are experiencing hardship and suffering.
